title: Large language model-generated patterns for epidemiological modeling: a multi-benchmark evaluation framework
abstract: arXiv:2610.15994v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Representing individual-level behavioral heterogeneity is challenging in epidemiological modeling, particularly when empirical behavioral data are sparse. We assess the potential of large language model (LLM)-generated behavioral outputs in addressing this challenge, using hepatitis C virus-related behaviors among people who inject drugs as a case study. Correspondence with epidemiological patterns was evaluated using external benchmarks: literature-informed association directions, correlations from an agent-based model (ABM), and survey associations. Across three LLMs, unconditional directional recovery across 28 retained literature-informed associations was 46-68%, compared with 82-93% agreement when LLMs were directly asked to classify the same associations. translated_title: 大语言模型生成模式用于流行病学建模：一个多基准评估框架
translated_abstract: 在流行病学建模中，刻画个体层面的行为异质性具有挑战性，尤其是在经验行为数据稀缺的情况下。我们评估了大语言模型（LLM）生成的行为输出在应对这一挑战方面的潜力，并以注射吸毒人群中与丙型肝炎病毒相关的行为作为案例研究。我们使用外部基准来评估其与流行病学模式的对应关系：基于文献的关联方向、来自基于主体模型（ABM）的相关性以及调查关联。在三个大语言模型中，对28个保留的基于文献的关联进行无条件方向恢复的比例为46-68%，而当直接要求大语言模型对相同关联进行分类时，一致性达到82-93%。与ABM和调查相关性模式的平均绝对差异分别为0.11-0.13和0.15-0.18。这些发现共同表明，大语言模型生成的行为模式与流行病学模式之间存在部分一致性。
tldr: 本研究提出了一个多基准评估框架，以注射吸毒者丙肝相关行为为例，系统评估大语言模型生成的行为模式在流行病学建模中的可靠性，发现其与经验模式仅部分一致，而直接要求LLM分类关联时一致性显著更高。
en_tdlr: This study proposes a multi-benchmark evaluation framework to assess LLM-generated behavioral patterns for epidemiological modeling using HCV-related behaviors among people who inject drugs as a case study, finding only partial alignment with empirical patterns, with notably higher agreement when LLMs are directly asked to classify associations.
